top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation is a new chemical design principle, event-driven pharmacology by induced proximity, in which designed heterobifunctional molecules bring a chosen protein to an E3 ligase. Crews and Deshaies supplied the concept and Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made it rational and drug-like, so the three-name allocation under a designed-degrader citation is clean. Mechanisms are reproduced across many laboratories; the lack of an approved PROTAC is a timing risk, not a scientific doubt. The Handa variant (P003) is defensible and ranked second, then C-N coupling (P001), which is mature but partly overlaps the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
